```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# reserves blank work space (no ruled lines); pair with fig.height
blank_space <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
}

# keeps a prompt and its answer space on one PDF page: place `r nq(...)` on its
# own line just above the prompt. lines = lines of prompt text, rows = rows of
# blank space below it (0.3 in each)
nq <- function(lines, rows = 0, extra = 0) {
  if (!knitr::is_latex_output()) return("")
  knitr::asis_output(sprintf("\n\\needspace{%.2fin}\n", 0.23 * lines + 0.15 + 0.3 * rows + extra))
}

# fill-in table drawn as a plot; "" leaves a cell blank
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, family = "serif") {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = family)
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val, cex = cex)
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}

chl <- read.csv("../data/ReservoirChlorophyll.csv")
library(splines)
B <- bs(chl$week, df = 20, intercept = TRUE)
pnll <- function(par, lambda) {
  beta <- par[1:20]
  -sum(dnorm(chl$log_chl, B %*% beta, exp(par[21]), log = TRUE)) +
    lambda * sum(diff(beta, differences = 2)^2)
}
check_val <- pnll(c(rep(1, 20), log(0.2)), lambda = 10)
```

**NRES 746, Week 13, Lecture 2: Spline by Hand (take-home)**

Name: ___________________________________________

**Due Monday, Nov. 23.** Work on your own. You'll need R for Parts 2-4;
try Part 1 on paper first.

A water utility samples a reservoir every week for chlorophyll *a*, an
index of algal biomass. Ice and wind cancelled 8 of last year's 52
visits. The data are log$_{10}$ chlorophyll *a* ($\mu$g/L) by week of
the year. The utility wants to know when the spring algal bloom peaks
and how big it gets, so it can time its treatment.

```{r scatter, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=3.6}
par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 0.5, 0.5))
plot(log_chl ~ week, data = chl, pch = 19, xlim = c(0, 53), ylim = c(0, 2),
     xlab = "Week of the year", ylab = expression(log[10] ~ "chlorophyll a"),
     xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i", xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = seq(0, 52, 4))
abline(v = seq(0, 52, 4), h = seq(0, 2, 0.25), col = "grey88")
points(log_chl ~ week, data = chl, pch = 19)
```

## Part 3: A penalized spline, by hand

Use 20 cubic B-spline basis functions, with the intercept built into
the basis:

```{r basis-code, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
library(splines)
B <- bs(chl$week, df = 20, intercept = TRUE)    # 44 x 20 model matrix
```

The model is $y_i \sim \text{Normal}(\mu_i, \sigma)$ with
$\mu_i = \sum_{k=1}^{20} \beta_k B_k(\text{week}_i)$ (the vector of all
$\mu_i$ is `B %*% beta`), and the penalized NLL is

$$\text{NLL}_\text{pen} = -\sum_{i=1}^{44} \log p(y_i \mid \mu_i, \sigma) +
\lambda \sum_{k=3}^{20} (\beta_k - 2\beta_{k-1} + \beta_{k-2})^2$$

`r nq(6, 3)`

**3a.** *(Recommended: no AI.)* Write a function `pnll(par, lambda)` that
returns $\text{NLL}_\text{pen}$, where `par` holds the 20 weights followed
by $\log\sigma$. Check it: `pnll(c(rep(1, 20), log(0.2)), lambda = 10)`
should return `r sprintf("%.2f", check_val)`.

Your value: ________

AI use (circle one): no AI / AI helped (e.g., debugging) / AI wrote the code

`r nq(6, 7)`

**3b.** *(Recommended: no AI.)* Minimize `pnll()` with `optim()` for each
$\lambda$ below, starting from `c(rep(1, 20), log(0.2))`. Use
`method = "BFGS"` and `control = list(maxit = 2000)`, and check
`$convergence`. Record $\hat\sigma$ and the penalty term
$\lambda \sum (\beta_k - 2\beta_{k-1} + \beta_{k-2})^2$ at the optimum.

```{r lambda-table, fig.height=2}
blank_table(
  headers = list(expression(lambda), expression(hat(sigma)), "penalty term at the optimum"),
  body = list(list("0", "", ""), list("10", "", ""), list("1000", "", "")),
  col_widths = c(1, 1.4, 2.6))
```

AI use (circle one): no AI / AI helped (e.g., debugging) / AI wrote the code

`r nq(4, 0)`
